newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks up slightly on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks up slightly on speculative buying.

text.p: Despite new central bank measures to bar foreigners from repatriating baht funds obtained from deals in the bourse, Thai stocks gained slightly in thin early trade on Thursday, brokers said.
The gains came from light speculative buying. Wall Street's overnight close at a record-high was ignored, brokers said,

"Turnover is still thin because of the lack of fresh news. M Sentiment remains the same as foreigners stay on the sidelines after the imposition of new cental bank measures earlier this week," said Witawus Charuchandr of Ekachart Finance.
The composite SET index rose 0.67 point to 522.07 on 521 million baht turnover at 0348 GMT.

New measures announced by the Bank of Thailand on Tuesday required bank custodians not to accept transfers of borrowed and unpaid stocks from foreigners and non-resident investors selling Thai stocks must remit funds in foreign currencies only.
Brokers said the lack of incentives prevailing in the market now would keep the market bearish throughout the day.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list in terms of value, unchanged at 144 baht. Property developer Noble Development debuted today, was at nine, down from its IPO price of 16 baht.
